state.decision: Library colours: the Colours tab of the Library panel (Figma B13, plan row 11.122), backend and frontend, asked BEFORE coding (claude, 26 Nov 2026).
state.facts: The Library panel lists a project's assets in a grid of cards with tabs Colours, Text styles, Layer styles, Backgrounds, Fonts and Assets; only Assets, Fonts and Text styles work today, the others are dimmed naming row 11.122. A project is a folder with one .gpx document; today it stores project settings and the Library's virtual folders, and it holds no colours. A graphic (scene) paints an object's fill or stroke with a ColorValue: none, a solid colour (red, green, blue, alpha, and the colour space the numbers are in: srgb, display-p3, linear and others) or a gradient; the setPaint edit sets it for the selected objects, refusing non-finite components or an alpha outside 0 to 1. A package pins the exact items a graphic used. What changes how a graphic LOOKS is never a user setting, and a library change must not be able to change a graphic that is on air. The Editor has no colour picker yet. Owner rules: a control that does nothing is dimmed naming the row; a value shown must be one the app holds; a refusal names its reason; library items belong to one project and are not copied between projects.
state.proposed: A library colour is a named solid colour stored in the project: an id, a name (unique in the project, ignoring case) and a colour with its space. The Colours tab shows each as a swatch card with its name and value; the selected card offers Apply as fill, Apply as stroke (to the selected objects), Rename, Edit colour, Delete. New colour: from the selected object's fill (keeping its own colour space) or typed as a hex value (read as sRGB). Applying copies the colour into the object: nothing links the object to the library, so editing or deleting a library colour never changes a graphic; the card says in how many objects of the open graphic the exact colour is used now. Gradients, layer styles and backgrounds are later items.

link.instructions: When a library colour is applied to an object, what is stored in the object?

criteria.A: A copy of the colour. Editing or deleting the library colour changes no graphic.
criteria.B: A reference to the library colour, so editing it updates every graphic that uses it.
criteria.C: A copy now, with a reference added later if the owner asks.

new.instructions: How does a person add a colour?

criteria.A: From the selected object's fill (its colour space kept) or by typing a hex value (read as sRGB).
criteria.B: Only from the selected object's fill.
criteria.C: Only by typing a hex value.

kind.instructions: What can a library colour be in this first slice?

criteria.A: A solid colour only; gradients are a later item.
criteria.B: A solid colour or a gradient from the start.

delete.instructions: What does deleting a library colour do?

criteria.A: Removes the swatch only; every graphic keeps the colours it was given.
criteria.B: Refuses while any graphic uses it.
criteria.C: Removes the swatch and clears the colour from every graphic that used it.

usage.instructions: What does a swatch say about use?

criteria.A: How many objects in the open graphic have exactly this colour now, since nothing links them (and says that is what it counts).
criteria.C: Which stored scenes use it, read from every scene.

criteria.A: Any text of 1 to 64 characters without control characters, unique in the project ignoring case; refused by name when taken.
criteria.B: Unique by id only; two colours may share a name.
